linkedin.about: Alexa von Tobel, CFP®, is the Founder and Managing Partner of Inspired Capital, a $900M Pre-Seed to Series A venture fund backing fearless founders solving the hardest challenges facing humanity. In addition, Alexa is the New York Times-Bestselling Author of Financially Fearless and Financially Forward, and she hosts Inc.'s weekly entrepreneurship podcast, The Founders Project. Prior to Inspired Capital, Alexa founded LearnVest in 2008 with the goal of helping people make progress on their money. After raising nearly $75 million in venture capital, LearnVest was acquired by Northwestern Mutual in May 2015 in one of the biggest fintech acquisitions of the decade. Following the acquisition, von Tobel joined the management team of Northwestern Mutual as the company’s first-ever Chief Digital Officer, overseeing digital strategy. She later assumed the role of Chief Innovation Officer through which she oversaw Northwestern Mutual’s venture arm. Alexa has appeared on the cover of Forbes Magazine, been interviewed on NPR’s How I Built This and been featured in a wide variety of publications from The New York Times to Vogue. She is a member of the 2016 Class of Henry Crown Fellows and an inaugural member of President Obama’s Ambassadors for Global Entrepreneurship. Alexa has been honored with numerous recognitions including: Fortune’s 40 Under 40, Fortune's Most Powerful Women, Forbes’ 30 Under 30, Inc. Magazine's 30 Under 30 and World Economic Forum's Young Global Leader. Originally from Florida, Alexa attended Harvard College and Harvard Business School before settling in New York City where she currently resides with her husband and their three children.

As an early-stage investor at Inspired Capital , the most important factor in an investment decision is the founder, not the brand. In the early innings of a business, I'd rather see a founder spend their energy getting in front of customers and nailing down product-market fit than perfecting a visual identity. Your logo will not save a product nobody wants. Your customers will tell you far more about your business than any brand deck ever could. But I don't think that means brand doesn't matter. It means timing matters. As AI makes it easier to start a company and lowers the barriers to entry, brand is becoming one of the few things that can actually help a company stand out. When anyone can ship a product quickly, the story you tell, the identity you build, and the trust you earn become real competitive advantages, not decoration. So here's my advice: don't confuse brand with credibility. Credibility comes first, from your product and your customers, and ideally your customers obsessing over your product. Brand comes next, and it should tell the truth about what you've already built, not paper over what you haven't. The founders I admire most treat their brand as a reflection of real traction, not a substitute for it. Get the fundamentals right. The rest can, and should, evolve. 600k+ downloads later and thats a wrap on Season 1 of Inspired! 🎙️

Want to learn from some of the biggest visionaries changing the future? This season we sat down with people bringing extinct animals back to life, founders going to space, builders reimagining safety for a billion people, and those rewiring the internet itself. Every conversation left us thinking bigger about what is possible - about how much better the world can be. ✨

Every guest is at the very top of their field, and we loved getting to share their bold predictions and contrarian takes on where the world is headed from their unique vantage point. 

Season 2 is coming soon, so if you are a founder building something truly unique, we want to hear all about it.

We also just launched our new YouTube channel, Inspired with Alexa von Tobel! Subscribe so you never miss out on new content. (Link in bio!) 🎧

In 2020, he looked us in the eyes and said that “one day you’ll wish you gave me $10M instead of $3M.”

That was Michael Brown, co-founder of @teamshares after he signed our term sheet— and he was right.

@teamshares is public on Nasdaq. TMS. 🔔

Six years ago: 5 people. 1 acquisition. Under $2M of revenue. A WeWork. A 200-year plan. We backed Teamshares on a draft idea and fell in love with their mission and potential. 

Today: 92 companies. $500M revenue. 30+ states. Thousands of everyday workers who now own a piece of what they built.

70% of small businesses in America never find a buyer when their owner retires. Teamshares was built to fix that — permanently.

Michael will be the first to say this is still the first inning to what they will accomplish. We believe him completely and have been honored to be on their incredible journey.
Congrats to Michael, Alex, Kevin, and the entire Teamshares team. Onwards and upwards. 🚀

We’re thrilled to announce the promotion of Annie Shapiro to Partner at @inspiredcapital. Alexa, Mark and Annie have worked nearly 17 years, side by side since she was in undergrad at Princeton.

Annie has been with Inspired since the *very* beginning and has built our Platform from the ground up. With her deep operating experience across the New York tech ecosystem, it’s no surprise that one founder described her as a “superhero who can morph her powers into whatever strength or skill we need on any given day.” 

She has produced our award-winning podcast for eight years, and through it all, she has been an advocate for the VC platform community, serving as VP of the Board of @vcplatform.

Beyond being an exceptional operator and partner to our founders, Annie is one of the most wonderful human beings. We feel lucky to call her a partner in every sense of the word! GO ANNIE!!! WE ADORE YOU!
